candidates.tagline: Pepsi's new body wash smells like cola — it's for your shower, not your glass
candidates.story: On July 31, 2026, Pepsi and cosmetics brand Glamlite launched a body care collection featuring a Pepsi Wild Cherry Body Wash and Vanilla Slushie Body Scrub in cola-dark packaging — because the company that makes drinks decided the next growth market is being rubbed onto your body.
candidates.why_funny: The marketing team looked at a beverage and said 'but what if you also wore it' — and then someone said yes.
candidates.alt: A Pepsi-branded Vanilla Slushie Body Scrub jar held in hand next to a Pepsi Wild Cherry Body Wash bottle labeled 'Wild Cherry Scented, Infused with Niacinamide & Vitamin B3', both in deep cola-brown packaging with the Pepsi logo, placed next to a white towel

candidates.tagline: Google let anyone deepfake cities onto real satellite maps — then panicked and killed it in 24 hours
candidates.story: On July 31, 2026, Google launched an AI image generation feature for Google Earth that let users prompt-generate fake imagery and superimpose it over real satellite maps; after critics flagged that this gave anyone a tool to fabricate evidence using 'one of the most reliable sources of visual evidence,' Google pulled the feature the following day — while it was live the disclaimer read 'Generative AI can make mistakes, so double-check it.'
candidates.why_funny: Google built a way to put photorealistic fake cities on real maps, released it to the public, and then noticed this was a bad idea at exactly the same moment everyone else did.
candidates.alt: Screenshot of Google Earth's AI image creation interface showing a prompt-generated futuristic fantasy city with glowing green hyperloop pathways, a massive transparent dome arena, and a spiraling tower, overlaid on real satellite imagery of a city grid, with 'Refine image' and 'Save to project' buttons visible and a disclaimer reading 'Generative AI can make mistakes, so double-check it'
